aciklama:
A mine is a hole holding up a mountain - and the rock is always trying to close it. Here is why mines fail.

#shorts #engineering #science #mining #howitworks

sahneler.metin: A mine is a hole holding up an entire mountain.
The rock above weighs millions of tons and wants to fall.
Miners leave pillars of rock behind to hold up the roof.
But take out too much, and those pillars slowly crush.
Water seeping in weakens the rock and rusts the supports.
A single failing pillar can start a chain collapse.
Then there is gas - a spark in a coal mine is catastrophic.
Modern mines use sensors to catch the rock groaning early.
Deep underground, the mountain always wins in the end.

vaka.ders: sensors listen for the rock before it fails
vaka.yanilgi: Mine roofs rarely fail without warning — rock often cracks and pops as the load shifts.
vaka.tartisma: Should mines leave more rock behind as pillars, even if it cuts output?

The Chain Collapse Miners Fear Most
